 Listeria Biscuit Recall Expands to Vending Machine Sandwiches and Gravy Meals Sold in Seven Southern States
 Published Nov 19, 2026 12:58 AM EST 
 By
 Joseph James 
 Editorial Illustration via AI 
 Share on Twitter 
 Share on Facebook 
 Share on WhatsApp 
 Fresh & Ready Foods LLC has expanded its Listeria recall to a larger breakfast sandwich and a biscuit-and-sausage-gravy meal sold through vending machines, break rooms and micro-markets in seven Southern states. The expansion was announced Nov. 17 and posted in an expanded recall notice on the FDA website on Nov. 18. It covers products distributed Oct. 15 through Nov. 11 in Alabama, Arkansas, Louisiana, Mississippi, Oklahoma, Tennessee and Texas.
 The products came from the company's Longview, Texas, facility and were made with biscuits from C.H. Guenther & Son, a San Antonio company that recalled certain biscuit products over possible Listeria monocytogenes contamination . No illnesses have been reported .
 The newly added sandwich carries Fresh Thru dates as late as Nov. 22, so some may still be in workplace coolers this week. Workers who buy breakfast from a machine may never see a recall notice, and Listeria symptoms can take weeks to appear, long after the wrapper is gone.
 Products, Dates and States in the Expanded Recall
 The first product is the Fresh To You Sausage, Egg & Cheese Biscuit Sandwich, 5.7 ounces, in clear plastic film, SKU 3100048. Fresh Thru dates of Nov. 12 through Nov. 22 are printed on the front label. It was distributed in all seven states.
 The second is the Mmm! Meals Made in Minutes Biscuit & Sausage Gravy, 9.5 ounces, in a clear clamshell, SKU 90013, with EXP dates of Nov. 12 through Nov. 18 on the front label. It was distributed in the same states except Alabama.
 The products went to employee break rooms, grab-and-go coolers, refrigerated vending machines and micro-markets, places that rarely send recall emails or loyalty-card alerts. The company said its Renton, Washington, facility has no affected products.
 Consumers should not eat the products and should throw away any that remain. Full refunds are available through RecallConcern@HotLineGlobal.com or 1-855-424-8390, Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 6 p.m. Eastern.
 A Biscuit Recall Moving From the Northwest to the South
 The Southern expansion builds on the company's first recall, announced Nov. 7. MedicalDaily previously reported that Fresh & Ready recalled 2,414 smaller biscuit sandwiches weighing 4.6 ounces each. Those sandwiches went to break rooms and vending machines in Oregon and Washington between Oct. 25 and Nov. 4.
 On Nov. 14, the USDA's Food Safety and Inspection Service (FSIS) issued a public health alert for the gravy meals , which contain meat, after a firm told the agency it had received recalled Guenther biscuits, News 4 San Antonio reported . FSIS warned that more affected products could be identified. The Nov. 17 notice turns that alert into a formal company recall of the meals and adds the larger sandwich.
 "There have been no confirmed reports of illness due to consumption of these products," FSIS said in its alert.
 Key questions remain open. The Fresh & Ready notice does not say which Guenther biscuit products were involved, how many units were affected, or whether Listeria was found in any finished product .
 Listeria's Long Delay and Who Faces the Most Risk
 Listeria is unusual among foodborne germs because illness can start weeks after eating contaminated food. FSIS advises high-risk people who develop flu-like symptoms within two months of eating a possibly contaminated food to seek medical care and mention what they ate.
 The recall notice says Listeria can cause serious and sometimes fatal infections in young children, frail or elderly people, and others with weakened immune systems. The CDC lists the groups at highest risk as pregnant women, newborns, adults 65 and older, and people with weakened immune systems.
 Pregnancy carries a special concern. A pregnant person may feel only mildly ill while the infection leads to miscarriage, stillbirth, premature delivery, or a serious infection in the newborn, according to FSIS.
 Symptoms can include fever, muscle aches, headache, stiff neck, confusion, loss of balance and convulsions, sometimes preceded by diarrhea or other stomach upset, FSIS says. Listeriosis is treated with antibiotics, and a lab test is needed to confirm it.
 Listeria can survive freezing and can grow at refrigerator temperatures, so the guidance is to throw the products away rather than store or reheat them.
 Checks for Workers, Employers and Vending Operators
 Anyone who bought a biscuit sandwich or biscuit-and-gravy meal from a workplace machine or cooler in the seven states since mid-October can check the front label for the product name, SKU and date. People who already ate one and feel well generally do not need testing, since most people who eat contaminated food do not become seriously ill.
 People who develop fever and muscle aches, especially those who are pregnant, older or immunocompromised, should call a clinician and mention possible Listeria exposure. A stiff neck, confusion, loss of balance, or a seizure needs urgent care.
 Employers, cafeteria managers and vending operators can pull matching items, post a notice near machines and clean shelves and coolers that held them with hot, soapy water.
 Questions about the gravy meal can also go to the USDA Meat and Poultry Hotline at 888-674-6854, weekdays from 10 a.m. to 6 p.m. Eastern. MedicalDaily will report any additional products, states, or illnesses tied to the recalled biscuits.
 Developing Story Timeline 
 Nov. 17, 2026: Fresh & Ready expands its recall to a 5.7-ounce sandwich and the gravy meal in seven Southern states. The FDA posts the notice Nov. 18.
 Nov. 14, 2026: FSIS issues a public health alert for the gravy meal.
 Nov. 7, 2026: Fresh & Ready recalls 2,414 sandwiches sold in Washington and Oregon, citing the C.H. Guenther biscuit recall.

 Key Questions Answered
 What was added to the recall? A 5.7-ounce Fresh To You Sausage, Egg & Cheese Biscuit Sandwich and the 9.5-ounce Mmm! Meals Biscuit & Sausage Gravy.
 Which states are affected? Alabama, Arkansas, Louisiana, Mississippi, Oklahoma, Tennessee, and Texas. The gravy meal was not distributed in Alabama.
 Which dates should I look for? Fresh Thru Nov. 12 to Nov. 22 on the sandwich and EXP Nov. 12 to Nov. 18 on the gravy meal.
 Has anyone gotten sick? No illnesses have been reported.
 How long after eating can symptoms start? Weeks later. FSIS advises high-risk people with flu-like symptoms within two months to seek care.
 What should I do with the product? Do not eat it. Throw it away and call 1-855-424-8390 for a refund.
